DISCRIMINATING: 'Phytophthora' vs 'Diaporthe'
Ruling feature : Location and appearance of stem lesion: dark brown basal lesion extending from the taproot upward (Phytophthora) vs. reddish-brown lesions at nodes in the lower canopy with sunken gray-brown cankers or linear rows of black pycnidia (Diaporthe)
Phytophthora: A dark brown lesion originating at the taproot and extending upward on the lower stem, capable of girdling the stem; associated with damping off, stunting, and yellowing.
Diaporthe: Small reddish-brown lesions near nodes in the lower third of the canopy expanding into sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins, and/or linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on mature stems.
Decision rule  : IF the stem lesion is dark brown, originates at or near the taproot, and extends upward girdling the base, THEN suspect Phytophthora; IF lesions are reddish-brown at nodes forming sunken cankers with reddish margins OR linear rows of black specks appear on mature stems, THEN suspect Diaporthe.

DISCRIMINATING: 'Green_stem_disorder' vs 'Diaporthe'
Ruling feature : Presence of linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) and/or sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins on stems

Decision rule  : IF the stem displays linear rows of black specks and/or sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins, THEN classify as Diaporthe; if neither feature is present and no description matches, Green Stem Disorder cannot be visually confirmed from available knowledge-base data.

DISCRIMINATING: 'Phytophthora' vs 'Green_stem_disorder'
Ruling feature : Presence of a dark brown stem lesion extending up from the taproot vs. no described lesion
Phytophthora: Disease A (Phytophthora) shows a dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending upward from the taproot, potentially girdling the stem and causing stunting, yellowing, and damping off.
Green_stem_disorder: Disease B (Green Stem Disorder) has no description available in the knowledge base, providing no visual markers for comparison.
Decision rule  : IF a dark brown lesion is present on the lower stem extending up from the taproot (with possible girdling, stunting, or yellowing), THEN suspect Phytophthora (Disease A); IF no such lesion is observed and the stem remains green, the presentation may be more consistent with Green Stem Disorder (Disease B), though confirmation is limited by the absence of a description.
